item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A is clearly preferable because its implementation follows the required repository path: it builds the multipart body with multipartbody.NewFile and delegates to FilesService.Add. Candidate B duplicates Add’s request, option, decoding, and error logic, directly violating the frozen contract.","reasons":["A preserves Add unchanged and calls s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), keeping option handling and error semantics centralized as required.","A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and the supplied filename, matching the established upload pattern.","A’s multipart test verifies method, path, multipart content type, field name, filename, file content, and decoded response.","A includes an end-to-end 429 retry test through FilesService.Upload, whereas B only separately proves that a generic bytes.Reader can be retried and does not verify Upload’s retry behavior or resent content at the service level handlers required by the report and contract tests overall (need semantics). .Actually the A handler’s second invocation does not re-read/assert the multipart body, so its retry test confirms a retry occurred but not that the replayed upload remained intact."],"risks_a":["No visible tests cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or propagation of source-reader failures, despite the contract explicitly requiring them.","The retry test counts two requests but does not validate multipart filename/content on the retried request, so replay integrity is not directly demonstrated.","The validation error combines two cases into one generic message; acceptable behaviorally, but less precise for callers."],"risks_b":["Upload reimplements Add instead of routing through it, violating an explicit frozen requirement and creating duplicated request/response/error machinery that can drift.","Its Upload test checks the field and filename but never reads or verifies uploaded content.","It has no end-to-end Files.Upload retry test; the added transport test uses a bytes.Reader directly and does not establish that the multipart helper’s body is replayed correctly after a 429, especially with streamed source content passing through Upload semantics in place of this generic reader test. .Actually multipartbody.NewFile likely returns bytes reader; hidden passes. But visible test doesn't connect the behavior end to end. Need concise no false claim. Could phrase no end-to-end retry test via Upload. Fine.No visible tests cover validation or source-reader errors."]}
